relevance_note: Case report of two infants with TNFAIP3 variants presenting with HLH: 'we report two children with the primary presentation of HLH, with a mutation in TNFAIP3, in favor of HA20'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON from values I typed and checked every span verbatim. Labels: the case sections are headed 'Patient one' and 'Patient two' (Table 3 calls them 'Our patient N. 1' / 'Our patient N. 2'; text also says 'our first patient'); the heading labels are used. Literature patients in Table 3 are labelled 'Table 3 #1' (Li at el) and 'Table 3 #2' (Takagi et al) from the 'Number' column; the Author cell is copied to source_reference_in_review. The Discussion text about Li et al.'s MAS patient [29] and Takagi et al.'s 7-month-old boy [9] is taken to describe the same two people. The three Zhang et al. 2021 patients [25] are included as 'ref [25] patient', ' 2', ' 3' because individual features are given; the paper does not print their variants or say explicitly that each has a TNFAIP3 variant (the paragraph is about HA20 patients), so they have no variant rows and disease label is not reported. The other three Li et al. patients ('four HA20 patients') are not described individually and get no rows. Patient one's healthy older sister is neither tested nor affected and gets no row. Patient two's parents were sequenced and are 'homozygous wild type'; they get rows ('parent of Patient two', '... 2', sex not stated) without variant rows. Variant notes: Patient two's protein change is described in text as 'a proline to leucine amino acid change (p. L275P)', which conflicts with the notation (L275P = leucine to proline); recorded as printed. Li patient's variant appears as 'c.C259T, p.R87X' in Table 3 and as 'c.259C > T (p.R87X)' with 'RS: NM_006290' in the text; table form recorded as original string and the text's transcript recorded. Patient one: zygosity, variant type, inheritance and parental testing are not stated; the abstract 'consistent with A20 haploinsufficiency' is not recorded as a pathogenicity class. Patient two: SIFT/PolyPhen-2 'probably deleterious' and CADD 29.1 are in-silico predictions, not recorded as functional evidence or author classification. Takagi patient: text says 'de novo mutation of TNFAIP3 was detected' but parental testing is not described, so inheritance is not reported. Patient one age at diagnosis = age when the WES result was delivered (2 years 4 months); age at last evaluation and age at death not stated. Patient two vital status 'alive' is from 'is receiving etanercept every 2 weeks' at time of writing. Possible inconsistency: text says Patient one had 'normal ESR, CRP' but Table 1 shows ESR 11 (range 0-10) and CRP 6 (range <6); feature rows follow the text (excluded) but the checklist item 'elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)' is left not reported for Patient one. Group statements naming 'our patients'/'Both of our patients' (MAS criteria; no positive autoantibodies; no symptoms of Behcet's-like or other autoimmune disorders) were applied to both index patients as 'inferred from group statement'. The broad 'no Behcet's-like or other autoimmune disorders' statement was not used to exclude specific checklist items (ulcers, thyroiditis etc.). Normal investigations recorded as the paper words them (echocardiography, CSF analysis, lymphocyte subsets, NBT, immunoglobulins); 'The skin appeared normal' (Patient two) is used to exclude the composite skin-lesions item; metabolic evaluation 'normal' and 'No other abnormality was found' were not converted into exclusions. 'Intermittent fever' was mapped to the checklist item 'recurrent fever'; a single fever episode (HLH fever, Patient two's prolonged fever, Table 3 'Fever') was not. Cerebral hemorrhage (Patient one) recorded as a feature but not mapped to 'central nervous system involvement'; HLH cytopenias not mapped to 'cytopenia (autoimmune)'. Table 3 '-' in 'Other features' for the authors' own patients is not defined as absent and excludes nothing. No stacked cells.
